passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril I, the 24th Pope of Alexandria, pp. 501–502
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL I, The 24th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — His Upbringing

This pope was given the title “Cyril the Great” and also “Cyril the Pillar of Faith.” Pope ‘Cyril I’ (Kyrillos) name is forever linked to the second great conflict about the theologies concerning the identity of the Lord Jesus Christ (Christology). St. ‘Cyril’ led the 2nd Ecumenical Council in Ephesus in the year 431 AD, which condemned ‘Nestor,’ the patriarch of Constantinople. ‘Cyril’ is reckoned as one of the outstanding fathers and theologians of the Church. The patristic understanding of the Incarnation owes more to St. ‘Cyril of Alexandria’ than to any other individual theologian.

His Upbringing:

Not much is known about his early life. His pious and wealthy grandparents lived in the town of ‘Memphis’ which was called ‘Arcadia’ (nowadays ‘Mit Rahena,’ south of Giza). On the death of his grandparents, an Ethiopian nursemaid who was heathen but heartily loved Christianity took care of their two children ‘Theophilus’ (Cyril's uncle) and his younger sister (Cyril's mother).

Once, the nanny took the two children along with her to visit the temple of ‘Artimus and Apollon.’ On their arrival, many idols crashed down for no apparent reason, and the nursemaid became so afraid. She fled to Alexandria with the kids, where she met with the 20th Pope St. ‘Athanasius.’ She was surprised when the pope told her about what happened to her in the temple, and she proclaimed her faith in the Lord Jesus Christ and got baptized, along with the two children.

‘Theophilus’ was eventually ordained as the 23rd Pope of Alexandria (385- 412 AD), and his younger sister was placed in a house of virgins until she got married to a pious man from ‘Mahalet el-Burg’ (Didoyscya), north of the city ‘El-Mahalla el-Kubra.’

Born between the years 375 and 380 AD, ‘Cyril’ got a great deal of learning in both the classical and theological knowledge, at the time when Alexandria was a great educational center. This in addition to what he was taught by his own uncle Pope ‘Theophilus.’ He was raised knowledgeable in the religious books, the Holy Bible, the sayings, and biographies of the fathers. He had, as well, the talent of memorizing the Church hymns by heart and singing them with his steady voice.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril V, the 112th Pope of Alexandria, pp. 527–528
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL V, The 112th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — Ordained as Pope of Alexandria (1874-1927)

Ordained as Pope of Alexandria (1874-1927):

After the repose of pope ‘Demetrius II’ in 1870, the papal throne remained vacant for four years and nine months, although everybody was expecting that Fr. ‘Yoĥanna of Paramus’ would fill it.

Finally, the ‘General Congregational Council,’ which ran the church’s financial affairs, presented a request to the government about his ordination. Then, Hegumen ‘Yoĥanna’ was ordained as a patriarch on the 1st of November 1874, by the name of Pope ‘Cyril V.’ The sons of khedive attended the celebration: ‘Ismaåil Pasha,’ ‘Tewfik Pasha,’ ‘Hussein Pasha Kamel,’ and ‘Hassan Pasha;’ along with a number of government ministers.

The Political Situation:

Due to huge accumulated debts after the Suez Canal construction, Egypt at that time was passing through a horrible political struggle. Khedive ‘Ismaåil Pasha’ (1863-1879) was exiled, and his son ‘Tewfik Pasha’ ruled in his place.

Both England and France took charge of the affairs of Egypt, which resulted in the establishment of an Anglo-French control commission in charge of supervising the country’s government, finances, and budget. They appointed two ministers (one British and one French) to be responsible for what was called: ‘Sanduq Al-Din’ (Public Debt Commission).

Before getting exiled, ‘Ismaåil Pasha’ formed a ‘Senatorial Committee,’ which had a patriotic spirit opposing the foreign control over the country, and everyone felt the responsibility as a patriotic Egyptian. Pope ‘Cyril V’ supported those patriots and encouraged them to help the khedive and counteract the British.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril VI, the 116th Pope of Alexandria, p. 534
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL VI, The 116th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — Ordained as the Pope of Alexandria (1959-1971)

Ordained as the Pope of Alexandria (1959-1971):

As the newly elected pope, according to the Church rite, was accompanied by the bishops from his monastery of the ‘Paramus’ to the patriarchate, on Sunday the 10th of May 1959.

Since his ordination, his door in the papal residence in ‘El-Azbakieh,’ Cairo, stayed open day and night before all. He chose disciples from the young men and had a diverse ministry.

On the Spiritual Aspect, he kept holding a holy liturgy daily with such spirituality and love that flared up the hearts of the people, drawing all to the love of God, the Church, and one another.

On the Construction Aspect, he started by reconstructing his beloved monastery of Mar Mina, which became a ruin in the 10th century. There, prayers, hymns, and monastic life resumed in that part of Marriott. He reconstructed, as well, the monasteries of ‘Scetis’ and those in Upper Egypt. He also laid the cornerstone of a new Cathedral and a ‘Clerical College’ in the region of Abba ‘Roweis’ in ‘Ăbbasiah’ Cairo, besides many other churches and convents.

On the Cultural Aspect, besides encouraging the Sunday schools, and ordaining two bishops; one for education, and another for scientific research, he set a particular building for the new printing machine, presented to him by the church in Austria.

On the Patriotic Aspect, the new pope chose to start his ministry in Egypt, by what the popes along the past generations used to do; he paid a visit to the head of the Republic ‘Gamal Ăbdel Nasser’ on the 15th of October of the same year.

There was an initial period during which ‘Gamal Ăbdel Nasser’ used to aim his hatred actively towards the Copts. At the time, the relationship between the pope and the president was taut. The pope’s only refuge was to cry out to the Lord and to seek the intercession of St. Mark, the preacher of Egypt.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril II, the 67th Pope of Alexandria, p. 508
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL II, The 67th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — Pope of Alexandria (1078-1092 AD)

Pope of Alexandria (1078-1092 AD):

After the bishops, the clergy and the archons discussed the election of the pope in the monastery of St. ‘Macarius’ for two months without coming to a decision, they moved to a neighboring monastery ‘Yuannis Kama,’ where they selected a saintly elder monk by the name of ‘Bisus.’ However, he protested that he was a common man unfit for that dignity and began banging his chest with a stone. He told them that the one who was worthy of this honor would be the monk ‘George’ (Gawargius) of the monastery of St. ‘Macarius,’ and that he was recommended by the reposed 66th Pope abba ‘Christodolus’ (1046-1077 AD). So the delegation moved back to the monastery of St. ‘Macarius,’ and they found ‘George,’ a middle-aged monk of great sanctity, from ‘Qalaqa’ in ‘Beĥeira.’ They settled on him as their candidate. They took him against his will, clothed him with the patriarchal garb, then they took him to Alexandria, where he was formally ordained by the name ‘Cyril II’ in the year 1078 AD. He was known as ‘The Sengarian,’ about the cell in which he dwelt as a hermit, known by the name ‘Sengara.’

He was ordained in the days of the Fatimid Caliph ‘Al-Mustansir’ (1029- 1094 AD), by a decree of a Council of the bishops and Archons held in Alexandria; and all the departments of the government well welcomed his ordination.

The new pope visited the Caliph ‘Al-Mustansir’ in his palace in Cairo, where he was greatly welcomed, and the caliph asked him to bless his mother, his sister, and the whole palace. The pope also visited the house of his vizier ‘Badr el-Din Al-Gamali,’ who issued a special decree for his administration to execute all the patriarchal wishes.

This pope sat on St. Mark's throne, while Egypt enjoyed complete peace, thanks to the rule of vizier ‘Badr el-Din Al-Gamali,’ the Armenian minister, during whose time Egypt enjoyed progress and prosperity. The position of the church thus became secure, after the hardships it had sustained under Fatimid caliph ‘Al-Ĥakim bi-Amr Allah’ (996-1021 AD).

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril II, the 67th Pope of Alexandria, p. 512
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL II, The 67th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — His Pastoral Works

Moreover, it is for all to admire the churches, the sanctuaries and the altars, and to forbid the laymen from entering into the sanctuaries.

One of the pope’s bishops by the name of Abba ‘Marcus’ took upon himself to organize the church readings during the services of the Passion Week, and he assembled a book on the consecration of the ‘Baptismal Font.’

Pope ‘Cyril II’ sent bishops to consecrate the Church of the Resurrection in Jerusalem when it was reconstructed after being burnt in the days of the caliph ‘Al-Ĥakem bi-Amr Allah.’

Pope Cyril II reposed in peace on the 12th of Paona 808 AM (July 1092).

[Fr. Menasseh Johanna: HIstory of the Coptic Church] [The Coptic Encyclopedia: Cyril II, by Subhi Y. Labib; p. 675-7]

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril I, the 24th Pope of Alexandria, pp. 502–503
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL I, The 24th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — His Upbringing

He was raised knowledgeable in the religious books, the Holy Bible, the sayings, and biographies of the fathers. He had, as well, the talent of memorizing the Church hymns by heart and singing them with his steady voice.

His uncle made him join the Theological School of Alexandria to study the philosophical sciences, which would help him in defending Christianity against the heretics and the innovators.

In the Wilderness of Scetis:

His uncle sent him, as well, to Abu-Maqar Monastery in the wilderness of the Nitrian Valley to become a disciple to Abba ‘Serapion,’ who was the disciple of abba ‘Maqar the Great,’ to teach him all the ascetic and ecclesiastical knowledge. During the five years that he spent with his mentor in the Nitrian Valley, he managed to absorb all the books of the Church, and God granted him the amazing grace of understanding, that by reading a book only once, he would be able to memorize it by heart.

Ordained as a Deacon, then as a Priest:

After all those studies, ‘Cyril’ returned to Alexandria, to his uncle, who commended his great early prominence and ordained him as a deacon. It so happened that whenever he started to sing the Holy Gospel in the church, with his incredible sweet voice, the believers wished that he would never stop.

Despite his young age, his uncle the pope ordained him as a priest and entrusted him to give the sermons, and ‘Cyril’ earned the admiration of the listeners, all the clergy, and the scholars of his generation for his thorough and comprehensive interpretation of the Holy Bible.

He accompanied the pope in all of his essential conventions, even to the ‘Oak’ (Sendian) Council, close to ‘Chalcedon,’ which condemned St. ‘John Chrysostom’ in the year 403 AD.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril III, the 75th Pope of Alexandria, pp. 515–516
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL III, The 75th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — Offending the Patriarch of Antioch

The pope consented to their opinion and remained in seclusion in the monastery of ‘Qasr el-Shamaa,(candle)’ until he reposed on the 10th of March 1243 AD. Despite the shortcomings of that pope, he authored many works about the Sacrament of Confession (the most important of which is a book entitled: ‘Book of the Master and the Pupil’); about the arrangement of Fasts, the Holy Sacraments and the laws of inheritance and the book consists of fifty-five discourses of a moralistic character.

It is noteworthy that the “History of the Patriarchs” curtailed his biography to a single page and those Coptic authors of the period, such as ‘Abu el- Makarim,’ the famous 13thcentury historian of the churches and monasteries in Egypt, overlooked his name completely.

After his death, the throne of Saint Mark remained vacant for more than seven years before the community found a successor in the person of ‘Athanasius III’ (1250-1261 AD).

[Fr. Manasseh Johanna: History of the Coptic Church] [The Coptic Encyclopedia: Cyril III, by Subhi Y. Labib; p. 677]

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril V, the 112th Pope of Alexandria, pp. 528–529
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL V, The 112th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — His Pastoral Activities

His Pastoral Activities:

87he most important one was establishing ‘The Clerical School,’ which he built on a plot of land he purchased in 1912 at ‘Mahmasha’ in Cairo. 88e completed the building of the magnificent Cathedral in ‘Azbekiah.’ 89e also established metropolitan centers in each of the ‘Hanging Church,’ ‘El-Ădawyya’ in ‘Bulaq,’ ‘El-Maåady,’ ‘Torra,’ ‘El-Maåsara in ‘Helwan’ and in ‘Temwah.’ 90e also built 13 new churches in ‘Cairo,’ ‘Giza’ and ‘Khartoum.’ 91e also established schools for the monks. 92n the days of ‘Ismaåil Pasha,’ the ‘Congregational Council’ was formed on the 2nd of February 1874.

The 1919 Egyptian Revolt:

In his days, the First World War (WW I) flared up in the year 1914, and at its end, the British Protectorate (guardianship) was proclaimed over Egypt- Sudan. Then, when the truce was declared in 1918, the Egyptians started to seek the independence of their land, and they revolted in the year 1919. In that revolt, the Muslims united with the Copts. After strife which endured for years, England abandoned its guardianship on Egypt on the 28th of February 1922. Sultan ‘Fouad’ declared the independence of Egypt on 15 March 1922, proclaimed himself as a king, set the constitution of the land, and established the parliamentary system under the leadership of the great leader ‘Saåd Zaghlul.’ Pope ‘Cyril V’ supported that movement all the way.

In his days, the status of the Copts was elevated, and they enjoyed their religious freedom and equality in the governmental jobs, trade, and the possession of the land. A category of prominent Copts appeared in both the wealth and political arena. The Christian teaching spread, and the echo of sermons was heard in the churches all over the land.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril V, the 112th Pope of Alexandria, pp. 530–531
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL V, The 112th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — More Pastoral Activities

More Pastoral Activities:

In the year 1911 AD, a Coptic convention was held in ‘Assuit’ to seek from the government to treat the Muslims and the Copts on an equal basis in all the civil and religious affairs.

During his papacy, he ordained for Sudan a metropolitan on ‘Khartoum,’ and built there a magnificent cathedral and seven churches.

The pope cared, as well, for establishing convents for women.

His Response to the Foreign Missionaries:

Pope ‘Cyril V’ cared for the church education, and he traveled to ‘Assuit,’

and there he exhorted the Coptic priests to draw the children to the Coptic Orthodox schools; and to defend the Upright Faith. All that because of the spreading of the American missionaries in Cairo, Alexandria, and Assuit. Since the arrival of American preachers in Egypt in the year 1854, they started to establish protestant schools and churches and to snatch the Copts away from their mother church.

Two Trips to Sudan:

In March 1904, His Holiness traveled to Sudan to be received there by the statesmen, the Muslim sheikhs and the Coptic congregation with honor and reverence. He laid the cornerstone for the Coptic Cathedral in ‘Khartoum,’ in the presence of the British governor of Sudan; the commander of the Egyptian army; Abba ‘Yoannes’ the metropolitan of ‘Beheira and Menoufia;’ Abba ‘Marcus’ the metropolitan of ‘Esna and Luxor’ and Abba ‘Pachomius’ the bishop of the monastery ‘El-Moĥarraq.’

In the year 1909, the pope visited Upper Egypt and went back to Sudan, where he consecrated the church in ‘Khartoum’ and laid the cornerstone of a tremendous Coptic school there.

Pope ‘Cyril V’ was a contemporary of the khedives ‘Ismaåil Pasha’ (1867- 1879), ‘Tewfik Pasha’ (1879-1892), ‘Abbas Pasha II’ (1892-1914), sultan ‘Hussein Kamel’ (1914-1917) and sultan/king ‘Fouad’ (1917-1936). His Papacy lasted for about 53 years, longer than any of the previous popes. He reposed in peace in the year 1927.

[Patriotism of the Coptic Church and its History, p. 384] [The Coptic Encyclopedia: Cyril V, by Mounir Shoucri; p. 679]

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril I, the 24th Pope of Alexandria, pp. 503–504
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL I, The 24th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — Defending the Upright Faith

Defending the Upright Faith:

In defending the Orthodox Faith, Pope ‘Cyril I’ was confronted with the following problems: 80he writings of ‘Julian’ the denier: who wrote three books against Christianity: “Against the Galileans;” in which he denied the Divinity of the Lord Jesus Christ; raised doubts in His sayings, teachings, and miracles. Pope ‘Cyril’ disproved all those claims. In the year 433 AD, he authored 30 books; ten of which are still in existence. Also, the pope wrote to the emperor ‘Theodosius II’ and sought from him to gather all the copies of ‘Julian's’ books and to burn them; and the emperor responded to his wish.

81- he followers of ‘Novatian’ the heretic: who refused the repentance of those who were forced to deny their faith during the persecutions. Pope ‘Cyril’ established the corruption of that view, and before the persistence of the ‘Novatians’ on their stand, the pope eventually had to drive them out of Alexandria.

82-

he revolt of the Jews against the Christians: Seeing the broad and swift spread of Christianity, the Jews committed actions of violence and murder against them. They claimed that a particular church was on fire, and then killed all the Christians who came to put it out. When the Christians retaliated by violent counter-attacks, the pope tried to oppose them; and not being able to do so, he drove the Jews out of the city without bloodshed, after having permission from the emperor, and that was the end of the Jewish community in Alexandria.

Because of his unceasing strife against what was left of paganism, the pope was falsely accused of killing the lady philosopher ‘Hypatia,’ who followed the Neoplatonism ideology, and was a friend of ‘Orestes’ the governor of the city. According to ‘Socrates,’ she was killed horribly by some Christians in March 415 AD. 83he most critical problem that Pope ‘Cyril’ confronted was the heresy of Nestor, the patriarch of Constantinople, who proclaimed that in the Lord Jesus Christ, there are two hypostases, two persons, and two natures. He claimed that Jesus performed miracles, being the Son of God, but he suffered, got hungry and thirsty, was crucified, and died, being the Son of Mary.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril IV, the 110th Pope of Alexandria, p. 525
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL IV, The 110th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — Pope Cyril IV Care for the Education of Girls, Family, and Children

He also put a condition that both the bride and the groom have to make a clear and personal proclamation of their consent and approval of getting married in front of the priest before he officiates that Sacrament. Also, he requested that both parties should be given an ample chance to study one another before they get married.

Due to the invasion of foreign missionaries to Egypt, the pope used to meet weekly with his people and the priests to keep them alert with his profound belief that the real reforms should start with the priest and would end up with the child, also it could work the other way around.

The Unity of the Churches:

The pope’s heart desire was to unite the Orthodox churches all together, so he did his best to get united with the Greek Church, which the Russian Church was part of. At the same time, he cared for his Church to keep her doctrines and traditions intact.

Having very good relationships with the non-Orthodox Churches, relationships founded on love and mutual trust with their heads, the pope was accused of seeking the protection of the foreign countries, which stirred up the rulers against him.

His relationship with the English Episcopal Church was perfect, and that Church had all intentions to help the Coptic Church to reconstruct the church and school buildings that have been destroyed by the ‘Darawish.’

Other Works:

During his days, abba ‘Basilius,’ the Coptic Metropolitan of Jerusalem managed to get a court decision establishing the right of the Copts to hold the possession of the ‘Sultan’s Monastery’ in Jerusalem with a decree from the Ottoman sultan ‘Ăbdul Majid I’ (1839-1861).

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril II, the 67th Pope of Alexandria, pp. 508–509
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL II, The 67th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — His Knowledge and Piety

His Knowledge and Piety:

Pope ‘Cyril II,’ has been of little education when he was chosen, did what the 12th pope ‘Demetrius’ the Vinedresser (188-230 AD) do. And he acquired so much learning on his own and was able to leave us a great heritage, which testifies to the depth of his knowledge. of God’s grace on him was that, when he consecrated the Holy Myron, it flooded over from the vessel during the prayers.

The King of Nubia became a Monk:

Shortly after the ordination of the pope, the Nubian king ‘Solomon,’ abdicated his throne to his nephew ‘Guirgis’ and chose for himself the life of seclusion in the monastery of ‘Nephrius’ located in the wilderness on the border between Egypt and Nubia. However, that monastery was seized by the Fatimid agents in ‘Aswan,’ in an attempt to annex it to Egypt; and they took the king captive and brought him over to the vizier ‘Badr el-Din Al-Gamali.’ The vizier treated him with deference, as a guest rather than a prisoner, and placed him in one of the state palaces. The pope and the archons of the Copts welcomed him with great joy. When he died shortly afterward, he was buried in St. George's monastery at ‘AI-Khandaq’ (known today as the monastery of ‘Anba Rowis’) with all the Coptic funerary celebrations.

That good reception and treatment of king ‘Solomon’ in Egypt created an atmosphere of friendship and brotherhood between the Copts and the Nubians. On witnessing, ‘Al-Gamali’ held a treaty between Egypt, Nubia, and Ethiopia to facilitate the trade between the three countries, in which the Copts played a vital role.

In the meantime, ‘Al-Gamali’ supplied the Copts with money to help to mend and reconstructing their ruined monasteries and churches.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril I, the 24th Pope of Alexandria, p. 503
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL I, The 24th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — Ordained as a Patriarch (412-444 AD)

Ordained as a Patriarch (412-444 AD):

Once St. Mark's throne became vacant by the repose of his uncle Pope ‘Theophilus’ on the 18th of Baba 129 AM (15 October 412 AD), the Coptic people and the clergy uttered their word and unanimously decided to choose Fr. ‘Cyril,’ the priest, to succeed him on the throne, just two days after the repose of his uncle. He sat on the throne on the 21st of Baba (18 October 412 AD), during the time of Emperor ‘Theodosius II’ (402-450 AD).

According to the Coptic tradition, the new pope visited the monastery of St. Macarius the Great, where he ministered the first Divine Liturgy after his ordination.

The Case of St. John Chrysostom:

As Pope ‘Cyril I’ was very preoccupied with the case stirred up between Pope ‘Theophilus’ and St. ‘John Chrysostom,’ he started his papacy by studying that case; mainly that he knew well that his uncle felt remorse just before he reposed for having to exile St. ‘John’ out of his throne. Finally, led by the Holy Spirit, St. ‘Cyril’ annulled the ex-communication of St. ‘John Chrysostom, ’ which was issued by Pope ‘Theophilus.’ Besides, he honored him by confessing his high status before all and commending the great value of his many works. During writing down the Divine Liturgy of St. ‘Mark,’ St. ‘Cyril’ included the name of St. ‘John Chrysostom’ in the ‘Commemoration of the Saints.' By doing so, the Pope ‘Cyril’ finally put an end to that issue.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril VI, the 116th Pope of Alexandria, pp. 531–532
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL VI, The 116th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — His Upbringing

The amount of material which has been written about this saintly pope in several languages after his departure was vastly more than what was written about him during his life. Many people in Egypt, Sudan, Ethiopia, Lebanon, and Syria got to know him as a man of God, a man of prayer who has the gift of performing signs and miracles.

After the repose of the 115th pope ‘Yusab II’ (1946-1956) on the 13th of November 1956, St. Mark's throne remained vacant until the 10th of May 1959; the day this pope was ordained. In that transition period, prayers, fasting, and counsels continued, seeking from the Lord to give His church a good shepherd. The election was held and of the three who had the highest votes, Hegumen ‘Mina the Recluse’ won. On Sunday the 10th of May, he was ordained, and was called ‘Cyril VI.’ Even though all expected him to be called ‘Mina,’ yet the new pope, having seen pope ‘Cyril V’ in a night vision, sought to be called by his name.

His Upbringing:

The child ‘Ăazer’ was born on the 2nd of August 1902 of a pious family, as the second of his siblings. The family lived most of its time in the city of ‘Damanhour’ after moving from the village of ‘Tukh el-Nassarah.’ Their house was the place where the monks used to find comfort, including an old one by the name of ‘Fr. Tadros el-Baramusy,’ who one day, told ‘Ăazer’s mother: “This child will be our portion.”

In Alexandria, completing his high school, he worked in a marine sailing company, where he suddenly presented his resignation, proclaiming his intention to become a monk. The family, together with Abba ‘Yoannes,’ the metropolitan of ‘Beheira and Menoufia,’ tried to make him change his mind; but he had already found his way to God.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Cyril II, the 67th Pope of Alexandria, pp. 511–512
passages.text:
Saint: CYRIL II, The 67th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA — His Pastoral Works

His Pastoral Works:

Pope ‘Cyril II’ made his relationship with Ethiopia, Antioch, and Nubia much closer; ordained Abba ‘Severus’ as a Metropolitan on Ethiopia, and ordained several bishops on many new bishoprics.

He cared to teach his people the Christian values, reading the Holy Bible and its interpretation, and supported the metropolitan of Ethiopia to put an end to the custom of having concubines among the Christian elites.

Of his great achievements was his preoccupation with issuing 34 Ecclesiastical laws for the clergy and the bishops, and sought from a deacon in Alexandria, called ‘Mawhoub ibn Mansour’ to do a census of the inhabitants of the wilderness of ‘Scetis.’

Among the laws issued by the pope and put into action, were the following:

 He put an end to the ‘Simonism’ in seeking the ranks of priesthood.  That the shepherd should chastise his flock by the cross, and not by excommunication, and not to bind nor absolve against the truth, lest, he would, himself be the one bound and excommunicated by God.  Any bishop who refrains from receiving a repentant sinner, will himself be excommunicated.  Every bishop has to visit all the churches and monasteries within his domain, looking after the priests, investigating their problems, and guiding them in their ministry. He should also care for the salvation of his soul, of those who listen to him and of those who work under him.  He drew attention to the duty of the church toward the poor; that the monks would never come out of their monastery except when allowed to do so by the pope or by their superiors, and that the clergy and the congregation should seek the judgment of the church and the bishops.

 He issued a law to commit the congregation to observe the fasts, to engage the clergy to care and honor the legality of the Sacrament of Matrimony. Moreover, it is for all to admire the churches, the sanctuaries and the altars, and to forbid the laymen from entering into the sanctuaries.

One of the pope’s bishops by the name of Abba ‘Marcus’ took upon himself to organize the church readings during the services of the Passion Week, and he assembled a book on the consecration of the ‘Baptismal Font.’

St. Cyril’s name is forever connected with the second great Christological controversy, which led to the Council of Ephesus (431 CE) and the condemnation of Nestorius. [463] He is reckoned as one of the outstanding Fathers and theologians of the Church. The patristic understanding of the Incarnation owes more to Cyril of Alexandria than to any other individual theologian. [464]

His wealthy and pious grandparents lived in Memphis, which was called Arcadia (recently Meet-Rahena in the south of Giza). On the death of his grandparents, the Ethiopian nursemaid who was heathen but heartily loved Christianity, took care of the two children Theophilus and his young sister (Cyril’s mother). She accompanied the children to the temple of Artimus and Apollon. On their arrival, many idols crashed down for no apparent reason, and the nursemaid became afraid. She escaped to Alexandria and met St. Athanasius, who explained to her what happened in the temple. She converted and the three were baptized.

Theophilus was consecrated Pope of Alexandria and his sister lived in a virgin’s community until she married a pious man from Mehallet-el-bourg (Didoyscya), north of Mehalla-El-Kobra. Cyril was born in Alexandria between 375 and 380 A.D, and evidently received his classical and theological training at this great center of learning in addition to the instruction provided to him by his uncle. He was very intelligent, gifted by his angelic voice in reading the Gospel and reciting the church hymns, in addition to his excellent ability for learning by heart the Holy Scriptures.

records.question: Who was St. Takla Haymanot?
records.answer:
St. Takla Haymanot was a prominent Ethiopian saint known as one of the pillars of Ethiopian monastic life. He lived from 1215 to 1313 and was a cause of salvation to many [1]. His father was a priest named Tsega Zeab, and his mother was Sarah (also called Egzie Haraya), who was taken captive during a persecution but was comforted by the Archangel Michael and promised a blessed child [1][2].

St. Takla Haymanot was born on the 24th of the month of Kiahk [2]. As a child, he was baptized with the name Fish Hazion, meaning "the Joy of Zion," and was raised in piety, asceticism, humility, and love [3]. At age 20, he was ordained a deacon by the metropolitan of Ethiopia, Abba Girguis II, during the papacy of St. Cyril III of Alexandria (1235-1243). He lived a celibate life even after marriage until his wife died, after which he was ordained a priest [3]. The Archangel Michael appeared to him, instructing him to dedicate his life to prayer, study, and teaching, and he was given the gift of healing and miracles. His name was changed from Fish Hazion to Takla Haymanot [3].

He preached against idol worship in Ethiopia, performing many miracles that led to the conversion and baptism of many, including a local prince and his family. He founded a monastery in the Amhara region, where he lived an ascetic monastic life and was regarded by monks as angelic. He was known for raising a monastery abbot from the dead and for his humility and love even toward envious people [4][5].

St. Takla Haymanot later moved to other monasteries, including St. Istifanos and the monastery of Abuna Aregawi on Debre Damo mountain, where he lived for 12 years. During his descent from the mountain, he miraculously flew down with six wings, which is why he is often depicted as a cherub with six wings [5][6]. He also traveled to Jerusalem and Egypt, receiving blessings and visions, and eventually returned to Ethiopia, where he had many disciples. He died around the year 1313 AD after being afflicted with the plague [6].

In summary, St. Takla Haymanot was an Ethiopian priest, monk, preacher, miracle worker, and founder of monastic life in Ethiopia, deeply devoted to God and the Archangel Michael [1][2][3][4][5][6].

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 4 — St. Takla Haymanot, the Ethiopian, pp. 218–219
passages.text:
Saint: TAKLA HAYMANOT, THE ETHIOPIAN, ST.

St. Takla Haymanot occupies a prominent standing in the Ethiopian Church as being one of the pillars of the Ethiopian monastic life. He lived during the years 1215-1313 and was the cause of salvation to so many. His father, the priest Tsega Zeab (=Gift of Faith), was married to a charming and rich girl by the name of Egzie Haraya (=Choice of God) or Sarah in Hebrew. They both lived a life of piety, loving the poor and the needy. Not having any children, Sarah sought from her husband to distribute all their possessions on the poor and to release all their slaves and maidservants. After asking her not to have them act in a rush on that matter, her husband, the priest, found her still persistent in her position. So, he rejoiced in her counsel and did according to her heart’s desire. The slaves and the maidservants were intensely grieved, for they used to feel as members of the household, and some of them sought to remain with them in the house as brothers and sisters, which they did.

When the pagan Matolomy became the king of Ethiopia, he started to persecute the Christians. He sent his soldiers everywhere around to apply their acts of violence against the Christians. One of the soldiers reached the house of the priest and planned to kill him with his spear. But, the priest managed to flee from his home and dived into a lake. The soldier stood by on the shore, waiting for him to come out of the water to kill him. After spending a long time waiting, the soldier assumed that the priest had already drowned. However, it happened that when the priest dived in the lake, he found the Archangel Michael covering him as though in a tent. Later on, when he came out of the water, he found that his wife was taken as a captive and the church was devastated. He then cried bitterly.

It happened that when the soldiers realized how beautiful the wife Sarah was, they brought her up to their king as a precious gift. He ordered them to keep her in one of his houses and adorn her with gold, silver, expensive jewelry, and magnificent attire. On the other hand, she abstained from the superb food, and her tears never ceased to flow. By night, when all went to sleep, she took off the precious attire and put on her simple garment, prayed to God seeking salvation from that evil situation. And, she asked the intercession of the Archangel Michael, whose feasts she used to celebrate every month, by giving many gifts to the poor. Then, God sent his archangel to comfort her and to give her the good news that she would be granted a child who would be a cause of blessing to so many.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 4 — St. Takla Haymanot, the Ethiopian, pp. 218–219
passages.text:
Saint: TAKLA HAYMANOT, THE ETHIOPIAN, ST.

And, she asked the intercession of the Archangel Michael, whose feasts she used to celebrate every month, by giving many gifts to the poor. Then, God sent his archangel to comfort her and to give her the good news that she would be granted a child who would be a cause of blessing to so many.

In the morning, she put on the royal attire and was escorted to the king who greatly rejoiced to see her. He rewarded the soldiers with precious gifts and sought from them to bring her to the idols’ temple to hold an official celebration of their marriage. The king came into the temple, worshipped before the idols; while she stood waiting for God to rescue her. Then, suddenly a lightning, thunder and earthquakes took place; and the Archangel Michael came down to carry her to the church, where she used to pray with her husband the priest.

On seeing how splendid she looked in her royal attire with her face covered with a veil; her husband assumed that she was one of the royal household. She revealed her identity to her husband and told him about all that God did for her. They both glorified God and gave Him thanks to His great mercies. In the evening, Sarah saw a lighted pillar in the middle of her house, with its top in heaven and embracing many diverse birds; and toward which many peoples and kings looked with marvel. The priest, on the other hand, saw as though a shining sun was underneath his bed, surrounded by many stars that shone on the whole universe. In that very night, Sarah conceived the blessed child, who was born on the 24th of the month of Kiahk.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 4 — St. Takla Haymanot, the Ethiopian, pp. 219–220
passages.text:
Saint: TAKLA HAYMANOT, THE ETHIOPIAN, ST. — His Childhood

His Childhood:

In the biography of St. Takla Haymanot, many events were mentioned about God’s work within him during his childhood. Among these was that: after his parents sold all that his mother Sarah brought from the palace of the king from splendid attire, gold, silver, and pearls and distributed their price on the poor, the land went through a severe famine, and so many people were suffering. The mother was crying bitterly longing to give something more to the poor. The suckling baby, seeing her tears, pointed his little hand toward a small cup of flour and touched it. The flour started to flow heavily from that cup. His mother hastened to bring all that she had in her kitchen for the suckling to touch with his hand to let her have plenty to give to the poor. The little child was baptized, and called by the name ‘Fish Hazion,’ (meaning: the Joy of Zion), to be raised in a life of piety and worship with a spirit of asceticism, along with humility and love for everyone.

His Ordination:

Having reached 20 years of age, the metropolitan of Ethiopia Abba ‘Girguis II’ ordained him as a deacon in the days of the 75th Pope, St. Cyril III of Alexandria (1235-1243). During the ordination, the metropolitan kissed him, declared that he would be beloved by God and that the angel of the Lord would always accompany him with a sword of fire in his hand. St. Takla Haymanot lived a life of purity and chastity; and when his parents urged him to get married, he refrained, proclaiming his desire to live a celibate life. However, when they forced him to do so, he lived with his wife like brother and sister until she reposed in the Lord. Then, the metropolitan of Ethiopia ordained him as a priest. His mother reposed on the 22nd of Mesra, and his father followed her after only four days.

This young priest lived in his parent’s house for another seven years. Then, it happened one day when he went out to hunt animals, that the Archangel Michael appeared to him and told him that such action is not befitting for a priest, but he should instead dedicate his life to prayers, to the study of the Holy Bible and teaching. He told him also that God has granted him the gift of healing of the sick and performing miracles, and that his name from now on would not be Fish Hazion, but Takla Haymanot. It was also said that the Lord Jesus Christ put His hand on him and blessed him after calling him to the preaching work and promised to be with him and support him. The saint then distributed all his parents’ wealth on the poor, bid farewell to the inhabitants of his city, and set forth to preach.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 4 — St. Takla Haymanot, the Ethiopian, pp. 220–221
passages.text:
Saint: TAKLA HAYMANOT, THE ETHIOPIAN, ST. — His Preaching and Monastic Ministry

His Preaching and Monastic Ministry:

St. Takla Haymanot set forth to the region of Katata, where its inhabitants worshipped the idols, the trees, and the sun. There, the people were stirred up against him, mainly that they heard the voice of the devil from the tree, their idol, seeking from them to send him away. As for him, he stood afar, faced the East, raised his hands, and prayed, asking God to destroy that tree. So, the tree was uprooted and moved toward the saint, and then the devil confessed publicly that he was leading the people to vanity. On his hands, God performed so many miracles, which caused many to believe and be baptized in the water of the River. The region’s prince was saddened by uprooting that tree because it was producing a high income for him. And, when he came to inspect it, he found out that the saint ordered to use its wood to build a church. However, the prince fell ill, and the saint healed him in the name of the Holy Trinity. This miracle made him, his wife Acrocina and his three sons, get baptized, and the children's names were replaced with Christian ones. Together with them, many other people were also baptized. His ascetic life merged with his preaching work, so he was a true hermit who spent most of the forty days fasting period in the wilderness in a robust ascetic way, to come back to his brethren and children to care for them with stronger love.

The people got so attached to him, but in obedience to the Lord’s commandment, he had to move from one city to another in Ethiopia, to preach the Gospel, and to oppose the idol worship and the works of sorcery. So, he faced significant troubles and opposition; but God supported him with the miracles and the healings He performed through him.

Besides his preaching work, he lived as a Father to so many monks. In the monastery which the saint founded in the Amhara region, he practiced the monastic life with the spirit of worship and watching the nights, in addition to serving the others and ministering to the poor. The monks of the area considered him as an angel and not as a normal human being. The monastery turned into a center of preaching. It was said that the Abbot of that monastery died, and he was bitterly mourned by all. Here, St. Takla Haymanot came to where the corpse was and prayed to God, who raised the monastery’s Abbot from the dead. The nephew of the risen man was a priest, and he came rushing to cry at the feet of the saint seeking his forgiveness. He confessed to him that he used to envy his uncle on what God has granted him of gifts, and how badly he was aspiring to occupy his place as the Abbot of the monastery after his death.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 4 — St. Takla Haymanot, the Ethiopian, p. 221
passages.text:
Saint: TAKLA HAYMANOT, THE ETHIOPIAN, ST. — His Preaching and Monastic Ministry

The nephew of the risen man was a priest, and he came rushing to cry at the feet of the saint seeking his forgiveness. He confessed to him that he used to envy his uncle on what God has granted him of gifts, and how badly he was aspiring to occupy his place as the Abbot of the monastery after his death. And, asked the saint to pray on his behalf, and commended him for his holy life and his love even for those envious people.

When the saint felt that temporal glory would chase him after raising that monastery’s Abbot from the dead, he cried out to the Lord to take him away from that place. The Archangel Michael advised him to go to the monastery of St. Istifanos (Steven), headed by ‘Iyasus Mo’a’ (=Jesus overcomes). He forsook the region of Amhara, until he reached the river, where the angel walked along with him on the water to reach that monastery.

St. Takla Haymanot dedicated his time to worship and making metanoias with incredible perseverance that the Lord allowed him to see the heavenly Jerusalem and the thrones of glory prepared for those who strive. There, he heard a voice calling his name, telling him that he would be counted among the 24 priests and was given a golden censor to raise incense with them, and to praise the Lord along with them. From that monastery, he moved to the monastery of Abuna Aregawi on the high mountain of Debre Damo. There, he met with Abbot Yoĥannes (John), the Abbot of the monastery and the spiritual mentor of Iyasus Moʹa. Abbot Yoĥannes clothed St. Takla Haymanot with the monastic Great Eskeem, and he remained there for 12 years practicing the ascetic life. Then, after bidding the Abbot of the monastery and the brethren farewell, they tied him to a rope to bring him down from the monastery on the top of the mountain to the valley below. However, during that process, the rope was torn, and everybody assumed that the saint would fall to his death. But, behold! They watched how amazing wings emerged out of the saint’s back to let him fly and get down safely. That is why he is often portrayed like a Cherub with six wings. Then, the saint kept moving from one monastery to another; and the power of God kept working with him and within him.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 4 — St. Takla Haymanot, the Ethiopian, pp. 221–222
passages.text:
Saint: TAKLA HAYMANOT, THE ETHIOPIAN, ST. — His Preaching and Monastic Ministry

That is why he is often portrayed like a Cherub with six wings. Then, the saint kept moving from one monastery to another; and the power of God kept working with him and within him.

It was also said that he went to Jerusalem, where he met with the 78th Pope of Alexandria, St. Gabriel III (1268-1271); he got the blessing of the Holy Tomb and the blessed sites, then headed to the wilderness of Scetis in Egypt. There, the angel of the Lord appeared to him and asked him to go back to Ethiopia. There, he lived and had so many disciples sharing his monastic life. And, when he consummated his strife, the Lord Christ appeared to him, to tell him that he was about to depart. Then, he was inflicted with the plague and reposed in the Lord around the year 1313 AD.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 2 — St. Ezekiel, the Hermit, p. 99
passages.text:
Saint: EZEKIEL, THE HERMIT, ST.

He was the father of the monks of the monastery of Libanius in Ethiopia. He was the 4th generation succeeding St. Tekla Hymanot.’

[The Ethiopian Synaxarion: 27 Baramhat]

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 4 — St. Yousef Ĥabib, the Deacon, p. 365
passages.text:
Saint: YOUSEF ĤABIB, THE DEACON

He also used to research in the libraries of the Coptic Museum and the library of the Patriarchate, etc. He even purchased a permanent train travel permit to go back and forth to Cairo twice a week for that purpose. He used to translate, research in the biographies of the Saints and their sayings, then returned home to publish them in small booklets, to the benefit of ministry, and for the improvement of the souls.

In his extreme asceticism, he used to spend all his retirement income on these tasks with joy, and save nothing of it for himself. The many books and booklets he published on his own did not bring him any funds. He always lived poor without any possessions, ascetic, and a hermit in his appearance, food, drink, and attire. And, in this, he lived until he departed from this world.

With the establishment of the church of Abba Takla Haymanot in the borough of Ibrahimieh, Alexandria; he considered it his responsibility and without hesitation, he took upon himself to minister in the new church. In all the Holy Liturgies and eves, he carried out the duties of the cantor and the deacon, with a steadfast spirit and self-denial.

It so happened once, during raising the evening incense, while the church was at its beginning, and her books were not complete; sometimes, they did not find a Holy Bible to read the Gospel of the Prime hour in Arabic. So, he simply took the Coptic Katamarus (Καταμερος) book and read to the people the Arabic Gospel, directly translating it from Coptic to Arabic.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Aptalmaos, pp. 229–230
passages.text:
Saint: APTALMAOS (The martyr) — With Fr. Dorotheos

With Fr. Dorotheos:

Obeying the counsel of saint Bebnouda, Aptelmaos disguised himself and set forth on his way, to find out that all that the saint has told him was realized.

Encountering Fr. ‘Theodorus,’ he gave him ‘Bebnouda’s message; he counseled him to go to ‘Arianus’ the governor of ‘Ansenah’ and confess the Lord Christ, to receive the crown of martyrdom quickly, instead of taking the long way of the monastic life.

His Martyrdom:

He did set forth to ‘Arianus’ and confessed the name of the Lord Christ, and was subjected to a diversity of tortures. Then, the governor ordered taking him to the west bank of the Nile, to a village by the name of ‘Tukh Al-Khil’ (nowadays a city of ruins north-west of ‘Taha’); there, they hanged him on a high mast, and left him for 9 days, until one of the soldiers pierced his neck. He received the crown of martyrdom on the 11th of Kiahk.

It was said that bee’s honey kept flowing from that high mast, and that honey healed so many of the sick. His body was buried in that spot, and after the persecution, a church was built over his tomb.

[St. Pavnotius the Syrian: Spirituality of Praise; 1975; pp. 128-130]

[Synaxarion of Rene Basset: 11 Kiahk]

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — Fr. Abd-El Mesih, the Ethiopian, pp. 45–46
passages.text:
Saint: ABD-EL MESIH, THE ETHIOPIAN, FR. — Da Malkan [This Is a King]

The bishop read: “But to the wicked, God says: ‘What right have you to declare My statutes, or take My covenant in your mouth; seeing you hate instruction and cast my words behind you?’” We were all terrified to hear him start to rebuke the bishop, saying: “Do you say to the thief: Do not steal, while you do?."

Fr. ‘Tadros’ also said that while the saint was in the monastery, preparing to go to Cairo to meet with Pope ‘Kyrillos VI,’ he asked for a cup of tea. On seeing one of the monks bringing it over, he jumped and rushed towards him, and we followed him. He said to him, “You do not know how to make a cup of tea.” Then, he poured so much water and salt into the cup; that most of the tea in it spilled out on the ground. He then drank from it, saying, “Now! It is the better tea.”

Then, he set forth to the ‘Rest House’; the bus stop on the desert road to Cairo, where he got on the bus. He carried no money with him to pay the fare; however, all bus drivers loved to have him on board. On arriving at the patriarchate, he wrapped the blanket around his body, put his sandals under his armpit, and entered to meet with the pope for a duration not longer than one minute. He told him what he wanted, and then he went back to the wilderness.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — Abba Bipha, p. 355
passages.text:
Saint: BIPHA, ABBA (The martyr)

He was martyred in the days of Emperor ‘Diocletian’ (284-305 AD) around the year 303 AD. Hearing about the persecution, he considered it a chance to enjoy the heavenly kingdom. With an inflamed zeal, he stood in the middle of the city to urge the believers to become martyrs with joy. A multitude gathered around him proclaiming their longing to receive the crown of martyrdom and outlined in a procession led by ‘Bipha’ himself. Once they reached the palace of the governor, they publicly proclaimed their faith. Accusing him of sorcery, the governor started to torture him.

The hand of God was with him all the way. When they pressed him with the hinbazeen, the angel of the Lord came down and broke it, and inflicted some of the soldiers with paralysis. However, with incredible love, ‘Bipha’ healed them. When he was placed on a bed heated by fire, the angel extinguished the fire. Provoked to anger, the governor ordered to chain him and take him around the town while being whipped, to make him an example to the others. He received all that with joy and gladness of the heart. When he was brought back to prison, he supported his fellow prisoners and held them fast into the faith. Then, he saw the heavens opened, and as though a person of light carrying a crown was calling him to receive it. On the next day, he was tied to the tail of a horse to be drawn and bruised. They finally cut his head off, and he received what his heart desired. The feast of his martyrdom is celebrated by the Coptic Church on the 24th of Toba.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Almachus, p. 139
passages.text:
Saint: ALMACHUS (The Martyr)

The story of ‘Almachus’ (Telemachus), the Martyr, presents to us a living portrait of the soul which does not endure evil and cruelty and offers her life to redeem the suffering in the Lord. This saint spent his monastic life in the East; then came to Rome at the time of the ‘Gladiatorial shows,' when thousands used to go to the arena to see the captives or the slaves fight with weapons against one another until death for no goal except to please those spectators thirsty for blood-shedding, while the arena turns into a human slaughterhouse. Those shows eventually turned into some entertainment, with some freelances, men, and women, risking their lives for some reward; some fought blindfolded, and thousands may be killed in one day to celebrate a Roman feast.

Seeing that horrible scene, the eastern monk did not know what to do, other than, in love, he went down into the arena, amid the gladiators, risking his own life and in vain he tried to stop them. Here, having spoiled the ecstasy of fighting, the gladiators gathered against him and killed him.

Instantly, Emperor ‘Honorius’ (393-423 AD), appreciating that loving heart considered him “the Martyr of Love,” and declared the cancellation of that kind of shows around the year 400 AD. He is celebrated by the West on the first day of January.

[Theodoret: Ecclesiastical History; 5:26]

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 4 — St. Theodore, El-Shotepy, the Prince, pp. 253–254
passages.text:
Saint: THEODORE, EL-SHOTEPY, THE PRINCE — His Martyrdom

His Martyrdom:

Despite the agreement between emperor ‘Constantine the Great’ (306-337 AD) and Emperor Lucianus I (308-325 AD) to give the inhabitants of the land their freedom of worship according to the decree of Milan in the year 313 AD; Lucianus kept on persecuting the Christians with the utmost violence until he was overcome by Constantine in the year 325 AD. During that period, St. Theodore was martyred after the pagan priests complained against him before Emperor Lucianus. Proclaiming his faith before the emperor, he was provoked to anger and gave his command to whip him until his flesh was torn off. Then, St. Theodore was placed in the Henbazin to complete the job. But the Lord continued to send His archangel to support him and to give him strength. Lucianus tried very hard to convince him by promising him with so many offers, all of which were rejected by the saint. Then, the emperor ordered to place him on an iron bed heated with fire, during which the Lord was glorified through him, that a multitude of the soldiers and the public proclaimed their faith in the Lord Christ and were all ultimately been martyred. The saint was then hanged upside down with heavy stones tied to his neck. Then, the Lord Christ appeared to the saint to call him to enjoy Paradise. Finally, his head was cut off on the 20th of Abib.

[Maged Fr. Tadros: The Biography and Miracles of St. Tadros El-Shotepy, 1982]

Notes: [1] ‘Shotep’ (‘Hypselis’ in Greek) is a small town in Upper Egypt, it is a nome capital (metropolis) near ‘Lycopolis’ (Assiut)…

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 4 — St. Tadros, Bishop of Bahnasa, the Confessor, pp. 214–215
passages.text:
Saint: TADROS, BISHOP OF BAHNASA, THE CONFESSOR

This saint Tadros (Theodore), was a bishop of Bahnasa and suffered so many tortures during the persecutions; however, he was not martyred. Hence he was called a Confessor. He wrote an article (mymar) about the discovery of the body of St. John el-Gohary (from Beig Ashroubah) on the 3rd of Mesra. That manuscript was written in the year 1449 AM (1732 AD), and it is kept in the library of the monastery of Mari-Mina’in Fum el-Khalig, [No. 51/4 Misc].

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 1 — St. Basadi, the Martyr, pp. 310–311
passages.text:
Saint: BASADI, THE MARTYR (The martyr)

The Coptic Church celebrates the feast of the martyrdom of the seven hermits of ‘Mount Tounar’ on the 29th of Paona. Their names were: ‘Basadi,’ ‘Cotolus,’ ‘Ardama,’ ‘Moses,’ ‘Esey,’ ‘Parcalas,’ and a monk with the same name: ‘Cotolus.’

The angel of the Lord appeared to the hermit priests ‘Basadi’ and ‘Cotolus,’ and urged them to seek the crown of martyrdom by confessing their faith in their Savior. At once, the two priests set forth to the governor, elated in spirit, anticipating their crown. There, they met with five hermits coming by ship to the governor to get their crowns as well. The seven got together with one accord, testified to their Savior before the governor, who tortured them, tied rocks to their necks, and cast them in prison.

Amid their suffering, the Lord Jesus Christ appeared to them to comfort them and to promise them with the kingdom of heaven. By that way, He turned their sufferings into a source of elevated inner comfort.

Then, the governor sent them to Alexandria to get a great deal more of torture. There, Alexandria's governor put them in pots filled with tar and brimstones heated over the fire. However, the Lord sent his angel and restored them to their perfect form. After all that much torture, when the spectators saw them alive and in sound shapes, 130 persons proclaimed their faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. They were all martyred in a grand procession preceded those blessed hermits, whom the governor finally had their heads cut off.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 4 — St. Shenouda, pp. 137–138
passages.text:
Saint: SHENOUDA (The martyr)

He lived during the 2nd half of the 7th century when the Arab invasion to Egypt has just begun. This saint was raised in a truly Christian way. He observed a lifestyle within God's commandments and guidelines. He did not stop at fasting, prayers and attending masses, but he was also a generous giver to the poor, and always visiting the sick and imprisoned. Some evil people were annoyed by his piety, so they went to the Arab governor, claiming that the saint was mocking their religion. So, they brought him over for questioning. St. Shenouda declared that he believed in Christ, who commanded his followers to love everybody. He explained to the governor that he was just doing that, and he never made fun of any religion. The governor did not accept his reasoning and ordered him to deny his Christ and join Islam. The saint refused to proclaim his pride in being a Christian. The governor put him through so many tortures, which he accepted gladly.

Finally, they beheaded him, and he received the crown of martyrdom.

[The Synaxarion: 13 Abib] [Iris El-Masry: The Story of the Coptic Church, vol. 2, p. 85]

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Vol. 4 — St. Sidhom Bishai, p. 144
passages.text:
Saint: SIDHOM BISHAI (The martyr)

On the 17th of Baramhat in the year 1561 AM (25 March 1844), the Coptic Church celebrates the martyrdom of St. Sidhom Bishai.

Sidhom Bishai was a trader of wood in the city of Alexandria. He used to go twice every year to Damietta to purchase lumber, which was imported through its harbor. Being an archdeacon who loved the old churches, Sidhom Bishai on hearing that the wooden roof of St. George el-Muzaĥem Church in the town of Basat in the district of Sherbin had collapsed; he took on himself the responsibility of repairing the damage done and provided a full ship load of wood for that purpose. At the same time, during his visits to Damietta, he used to attend the Holy Liturgies in St. George Church. One time, it happened that a non-Christian stroked shoulder against him on his way to the church aiming to block him from going to the Church. But, seeing how muåallem Sidhom Bishai paid little attention to that evil man, he was provoked to anger and paid some street boys to insult him. Then, it happened that the Mofti of the town was passing by; and these boys falsely accused Sidhom Bishai of insulting Islam, its “Prophet” and the “Quran.” Those false accusations, finding the expected fertile soil in the Moftis ears; he chose two of equally evil people around as witnesses. Through these people, they rigged the case against muåallem Sidhom Bishai. He was then 40 years of age, well known for meekness, kind-hearted and loving for all, not at all expected to utter what they falsely claimed that he has done.

records.question: Who was St. Simeon the Stylite?
records.answer:
St. Simeon the Stylite was a unique and unusual saint known for his extraordinary ascetic lifestyle and deep spirituality. He was born in 390 AD in Sisan, near Aleppo in northern Syria, to parents John and Martha. From a young age, he showed signs of holiness, including a dream in which St. John the Baptist announced his birth and future [2].

Initially a shepherd, Simeon was deeply moved by the teachings of Jesus, especially the Beatitudes, which led him to pursue a life of asceticism and prayer. He joined the monastery of Euzebona, where he was ordained a monk and became a disciple of Fr. Heliodore for ten years. During his monastic life, he practiced severe fasting and prayer, even losing and then regaining his eyesight through prayer [3].

Due to his extreme ascetic practices, including binding a rope tightly around his waist causing wounds, other monks asked the abbot to send him away. Simeon left the monastery to live in solitude in a dry well and later in a deserted area, where he fasted for 40 days annually and practiced intense prayer and contemplation, often sitting on high mountains with his eyes fixed on heaven [5].

St. Simeon became famous for living on a pillar (stylite means "pillar-dweller"), which he raised to about 30 cubits (52 feet) high with a small platform on top. He spent many years on this pillar, praying, preaching, and giving counsel. His holiness and miracles attracted people from various regions, including kings, bishops, and common folk, who sought his prayers and advice. He was known for his humility, compassion, and firmness in spiritual matters [1][8][11].

He endured much physical suffering and lived for 70 years, passing away in 459 AD. His death was marked by a grand procession including the patriarch of Antioch, bishops, army leaders, and thousands of soldiers. Many miracles were reported at his funeral [4].

His disciple Theodoret wrote his biography, witnessing his life firsthand. St. Simeon was called "The Wonder of the World" and was honored by believers and non-believers alike, including Persians, Midianites, and Ethiopians. He was a man of deep prayer, humility, and spiritual fatherhood, counseling kings and church leaders and reconciling adversaries [1][8][9].

In summary, St. Simeon the Stylite was a remarkable ascetic who lived atop a pillar for decades, devoted to prayer, fasting, preaching, and spiritual guidance, leaving a lasting impact on the Church and many peoples [1][2][3][4][5][8][9][11].
